methodGraph.rationale: Timeboxing creates clear, repeatable slots that turn the chaotic start‑up phase into a habit, helping you move from scattered to consistent. By limiting each block, you curb impulsivity and comparison, letting self‑acceptance and resilience grow within a focused, healthy routine.

activities.title: Morning Timebox Walk
activities.description: Set a 30‑minute timer, choose a simple intention (e.g., breathe, observe surroundings), and walk outdoors while staying within the timebox to build courage and consistency.

activities.title: Park Sketching Timebox
activities.description: Bring a sketchpad to a nearby park, set a 45‑minute timer, and create a visual piece focusing on one theme, reinforcing focus and resilience through kinesthetic art making.

activities.title: Visual Timebox Board Creation
activities.description: Use sticky notes or a whiteboard to map out the day’s tasks into colored timeblocks, then follow the schedule, supporting visual learners and reducing indecision.

activities.title: Focused Reading Sprint
activities.description: Choose a personal‑development article or chapter, set a 40‑minute timer, read without distraction, then note one actionable insight to reinforce self‑acceptance.
